# Kinds, levels and near misses

Every problem the change engine finds is data: a kind, and a level its kind fixes (Must fix, Check, or said); problems group by kind, one answer covers a group, and a name one letter out is asked about, never guessed.

## The rule

Every problem `planChanges` finds is an **issue** with a **kind**, and the kind fixes its **level**:

- **Must fix** (`must`): Faro can't record it truthfully. Nothing is saved while one is left, unless its rows are left out by an answer. Kinds: `required-empty`, `not-a-number`, `formula`, `precision`, `impossible-number`, `unknown-word`, `unknown-ref`, `ambiguous-ref`, `conflicting-refs`, `bad-key`, `duplicate`, `type-unclear`, `plan-order`, `stage-format`, `week-wrong`, `checkin-incomplete`, `cant-change`, `not-allowed`, `removal-refused`, `loop`.
- **Check** (`check`): possible but unlikely. It is a question; the change saves once it is answered. Kinds: `near-ref`, `near-word`, `near-header`, `new-team`, `same-person`, `same-goal`, `other-goal`, `other-workspace`, `past-stage`, `past-plan`, `odd-number`, `plan-question`, `no-unit`, `decimal-comma`, `replaces-others`, `many-admins`, `totals-row`, `big-removal`, `feeds-lower`.
- **Said** (`note`): how a row was read (an owner matched by name, a type read from the columns, a date read as a week). Never blocks.

An issue carries its sheet and row, the record's name, its column in the sheet's own words, what the cell said (`found`), the near match offered (`suggest`), the sentence for that one row (`message`: what is wrong, what was read, what would be right), the answers its group takes, and its group's id. Issues are listed in the file's order: sheet (Goals, Plan, Check-ins, People), then row.

**Groups.** Issues group by kind, sheet, column and the folded value found: the group's id is those four, so it is the same for the same problem in a corrected file and an answer given to one file still applies. Each group has a title (what is wrong, or its question, with its count), where its rows are ("Goals, rows 2 to 4 and 9"; past three runs, the first three and "and 12 more"), and its answers, the suggested one first and none chosen. Must fix comes first, then Check, then what was read; within a level, the largest group first.

**Answers.** `answers` maps a group's id to a choice (and a value where the choice needs one). One answer covers every row in the group: `use` reads the cell as the near match; `choose` with a value reads it as that; `new` adds a team (admins only); `leave` leaves those rows out (listed in `leftOut`); `last` or `first` says which of two rows for one record to use; `keep` gives goals the decimal places their check-ins were typed with (a Decimals change their owner or an admin may make); `done`, `not-done` or `from-now` settles stages already past (done records them in their due weeks, as setting up a goal does; from now counts them from this week); `right`, `yes`, `replace`, `add`, `new`, `same`, `change` or `goal` say the row means what it says. `confirm` (the older single switch) answers every plan question and every unlikely number yes. The commit is null while a Must fix or an unanswered Check is left.

**Near misses.** A name or word is folded before it is compared: lower case, accents off, "&" and "and" the same, punctuation and repeated spaces one space (so "CI CD" is CI/CD). Folded equal to exactly one candidate, it is that one. Otherwise, exactly one candidate within one edit (two from 8 folded characters; a swap of two letters is one edit) is a **near miss**, asked as a Check with the near match first; never for one or two characters, and never when two candidates are within reach. Nothing near is Must fix. Teams, people (names, and an email's part before @ at the same domain), goals, a stage's name and a column's words are all read this way.

**Defaults that are asked or said.** A new goal with no Type is read from the columns it fills in (Start and Target: a number goal; Limit: a range; Stages: a stages goal); none, or two of them, is Must fix. A new number goal has no unit unless the row gives one, and none is asked once a file. A new range has no warning margin unless the row gives one. A date in the cycle, in Week, Due week or a stage's week, is read as its week and said; one outside the cycle is Must fix. The due week is always checked against the start the goal will have.

**Never guessed:** an owner from a first name; one of several people or goals with one name; a number from text; a type from two groups of columns; a week from a date outside the cycle; a row whose key names a goal with another name, owner and team (it is asked); anything on behalf of someone who may not make the change.

## Worked examples

Each is run against the real rule by `src/spec/spec.test.ts`: the result is what the code gives.

| Given | The rule gives |
|---|---|
| Near misses: “Platfrom” among Platform and CI/CD; “CI CD”; “Platfrom” among Platform and Platforms; “vp” among the levels; “numbr” among the types and their other spellings. | `near Platform / exact CI/CD / none / none / near number` |
| Where rows 2, 3, 4 and 9 of Goals are. | `Goals, rows 2 to 4 and 9` |
| Amara loads 14 new goals whose Team says “CI/DC”; then the same file with the answer “use”. | `check: 14 rows name a team that isn’t here: “CI/DC”. Did you mean CI/CD? (14 rows, 1 group) → 14 new goals, ready to save` |
| A Goals row for G-1 whose Level says “vp”. | `must unknown-word: Level says “vp”. Use north star, svp or team.` |
| A new goal whose Type says “numbr”. | `check near-word: Type says “numbr”. Read it as number?` |
| A new goal with Start and Target but no Type and no Unit column. | `Type: metric (from Start and Target; the row gave none). / check no-unit: This number has no unit. Is it a plain count?` |
| A new goal owned by “Rhea Kapor”. | `check near-ref: “Rhea Kapor” isn’t here. Did you mean Rhea Kapoor?` |
| G-1 on rows 2 and 3 of one file. | `must duplicate (row 2), must duplicate (row 3): Key G-1 is on rows 2 and 3. Give each goal one row.` |
| A row called TOTAL with no owner. | `check totals-row: Row 2 is called “TOTAL” and has no owner. It looks like a totals row.` |
| A new stages goal with stages due in weeks 2 and 50, in week 45; then answered “They’re done”. | `check past-stage: 1 stage of “Runbooks rewritten” is due before this week (week 45): Draft@2. Is it done? → 1 new goal, 1 check-in (1 for past weeks)` |

## Not self-explanatory

- **Not self-explanatory:** A group’s id is its kind, sheet, column and folded value found, written with hyphens for spaces and colons between (`near-ref:goals:team:ci-dc`): a rebuild may make ids its own way, as long as the same problem gives the same id. The titles of groups are Faro’s wording; the conformance rows (spec/conformance/import.csv) score the kind, level, group and the one row’s sentence.
- **Not self-explanatory:** IM3 rewrites the preview around these groups; until then the preview lists Must fix by row and asks each Check as a group. near-header and other-workspace (reading the file’s headers and its Start here sheet) come with IM5 and IM3; new-team’s set-up case with ST4.

## Where it lives

- [src/domain/problemLevels.ts](../../../src/domain/problemLevels.ts): `fold`, `near`, `editDistance`, `levelOf`, `MUST_KINDS`, `CHECK_KINDS`, `NOTE_KINDS`, `issueOf`, `groupId`, `groupIssues`, `groupTitle`, `whereText`, `ANSWERS`
- [src/domain/changeset.ts](../../../src/domain/changeset.ts): `planChanges`

## Requirements

- `IMPORT-LEVELS`: Every problem an import finds is Must fix, Check or fine. Must fix blocks saving; a Check is a question that must be answered; a problem is said once per kind with its count, and one answer covers every row with the same question. A near miss is asked about, never guessed and never silently refused.
